title: CITE: Anytime Valid Statistical Inference in LLM Self-Consistency
claim: A stopping rule certifies a target as the unique mode by combining three simple checks on an observed categorical distribution, with error controlled at any time.
layout: Single panel: bar chart left, rule box top-center, e-process inset right, arrows pointing inward
description: A bar chart of an observed categorical distribution over LLM answer categories fills the left side. The tallest orange bar is the target r. Next to it is a dark green runner-up bar a, followed by lighter green bars. After those come dashed light-blue bars for unseen categories, ending in an ellipsis. A green double-headed arrow labeled 1 marks the gap between target and runner-up. An orange arrow labeled 2 points at the top of the target bar. A blue bracket labeled 3 spans the unseen categories. A peach box titled 'CITE stopping rule' lists three color-coded conditions: large pairwise difference, large target probability, and small unseen probability. Gray arrows link the box to a gray inset titled 'Anytime-valid inference by e-processes'. The inset plots error rising over time against a red dashed threshold ε. The eye goes first to the bars and the numbered callouts.
caption: Overview of the stopping rule by CITE. With the countably infinite set of categories A, CITE tests the hypothesis of whether the target category r ∈A is a mode or not.
abstract: Large language models often improve reasoning by sampling multiple outputs and aggregating their final answers, but precise and efficient control of error levels remains a challenging task. In particular, deciding when to stop sampling remains difficult when the stopping rule is data-dependent and the set of possible answers is not known in advance. We study anytime-valid certification of a prespecified target answer as the unique mode of the model's response distribution, a guarantee distinct from answer correctness. We propose the Certification by Intersection-union Testing with E-processes (CITE) algorithm, which provably controls false certification at any prescribed level under arbitrary data-driven stopping, without requiring prior knowledge of the answer category set. We also prove an category-set-size-free stopping-time rate, establish matching minimax lower bounds up to constants in the main regime, and extend the construction to confidence-weighted voting. Simulations and LLM self-consistency experiments show empirical error control and improved certification in diffuse-tail settings.
